title: Annotatio II §.IX close (5): Determination aporiae — spiritual presence in the believer’s soul, not in bread; stop before Annotatio III
pass_a_gloss: Finally (5) Consubstantiation is adverse to the Determination of both the internal quality and the external condition of Christ’s body, under which it is to be believed corporally present in the bread, and once to have been in the first Institution, and still now to be in every administration of the supper — for example: Whether emptied and crucified? or exalted and glorified? Whether joined to a rational soul? or separated from this soul? Whether swollen with blood? or bloodless? Whether as in the bread with blood, so blood in the wine with body? Whether in each part of the Supper, i.e. each species, both bread and wine, the whole? or a part of the whole? With determination doubtful at once, and yet ending no otherwise than if we confess Christ’s body present indeed, yet not corporally, but only supernaturally and spiritually present in the Supper — not in the bread, but in the soul of the believer alone who eats with true faith.
pass_b_english: (5) Consubstantiation cannot settle the body’s internal quality or external condition if it is corporally in the bread — emptied or exalted? with soul or without? bloody or bloodless? whole in each species or part?
The doubt ends only if we confess the body present in the Supper supernaturally and spiritually — not in the bread, but in the soul of the true-faith eater alone.
source_text: Denique (5) Consubstantiatio adversa est Determinationi tam qualitatis internæ, quàm conditionis externæ corporis Christi, sub qua, in pane, corporaliter præsens, & olim, in prima Institutione fuisse, & modò, in omni cœnæ administratione, adhuc esse, credendum est, puta: Num exinanitum & crucifixum? an verò exaltatum & glorificatum? Num animæ rationali junctum? an verò ab hac anima separatum? Num sanguine turgidum; an verò exsangue? Num uti in pane cum sanguine, ita sanguis in vino cum corpore? Num in utraque Coenæ parte, i. e. specie utraque, tàm panis, quàm vini, totum? an pars totius? Dubio determinationis protinus, nec aliter tamen, terminando, quàm si corpus Christi præsens quidem, non tamen corporaliter, verum supernaturaliter ac spiritualiter duntaxat in Coena præsens, sed non in pane, verùm in anima solius credentis ac vera fide manducantis, confiteamur.
